title: VACUUM, Autovacuum & ANALYZE
description: Understand dead tuple reclamation, MVCC cleanup, freeze maps, transaction ID wraparound, and autovacuum tuning.

data.text: Because of MVCC, updating a row in PostgreSQL writes a new row version (tuple) and marks the old version as dead. **`VACUUM`** reclaims the physical space occupied by dead tuples, making it available for new writes, and updates the visibility map. **`ANALYZE`** collects table statistics used by the query planner.

By default, autovacuum triggers when 20% of a table's rows have been updated or deleted. On a 100-million row table, that means waiting for 20 million dead tuples before vacuuming! Tune autovacuum on high-velocity tables individually.

data.title: Aggressive Autovacuum Table Settings
data.content: Triggering autovacuum at 5% threshold instead of default 20%.

data.text: Every transaction gets a 32-bit id, and after about two billion transactions the counter wraps. To survive wraparound, `VACUUM` freezes old tuples by replacing their transaction id with a special FrozenXID that is always considered visible. If freezing falls behind, PostgreSQL refuses new writes and requires an offline vacuum to avoid data loss. This is why monitoring for the oldest unfrozen transaction is a production necessity.

data.title: Check wraparound pressure and reclaim space
data.content: `age(datfrozenxid)` is the number of transactions since the oldest unfrozen id; approaching `autovacuum_freeze_max_age` means you are behind.
data.code:
-- How close is this database to wraparound?
SELECT
    datname,
    age(datfrozenxid) AS xid_age,
    current_setting('autovacuum_freeze_max_age') AS freeze_max_age
FROM pg_database
ORDER BY xid_age DESC;

-- Reclaim space to the OS (locks the table, rewrites it)
VACUUM FULL orders;

-- Cheaper alternative: rebuild a bloat-heavy table online
-- with a new table + logical swap, or pg_repack

data.title: VACUUM FULL is not routine maintenance
data.text: Plain `VACUUM` marks space reusable but does not return it to the operating system, and it runs concurrently with reads and writes. `VACUUM FULL` rewrites the entire table into a new file and takes an `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` lock, so it blocks all access for the duration. On a large production table, use `pg_repack` or an online table rebuild instead. Reaching for `VACUUM FULL` on a busy table is a classic outage story.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: `VACUUM` marks dead tuples as reusable space; it does not lock tables.
`VACUUM FULL` rewrites the table to reclaim disk space, but takes an exclusive lock.
Autovacuum prevents transaction ID (XID) wraparound, which would force the database into read-only mode.
